newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb on train wounds 40 in Algiers - residents.
newsitem.headline: Bomb on train wounds 40 in Algiers - residents.

text.p: A bomb on Wednesday wounded about 40 people aboard a train in the south Algiers suburb of El Harrach, residents said.

The attack came two days after another bomb killed three people in Algeria's southern city of M'Sila and two reported massacres in isolated villages in which more than 60 people were thought to have died, El Watan newspaper said.
"The blast went off inside a railway coach, part of a train coming from Rouiba to Algiers this morning," one resident told Reuters by telephone.
"The explosion occurred about a km (half mile) from El Harrach station."
Local journalists who visited the site shortly afterwards said the authorities had rapidly cleared the site and "we found no sign of any explosion", said one.
Several bombs have exploded on trains and been blamed by officials on Moslem rebels trying to topple the government.
The last serious train attack killed 21 people and wounded 20 in the south Algiers suburb of Gue de Constantined in April.
There was no official confirmation of the latest attacks by the authorities.
Earlier on Wednesday, El Watan, usually well-informed on security issues, reported the M'Sila bomb and massacres but appeared hesitant to give exact figures for the village raids.
The newspaper said about 30 Moslem guerrillas attacked Dairat Labguer hamlet near M'Sila town, 180 km (110 miles) south of Algiers, last week.

"According to eyewitnesses, the massacre reportedly left about 50 people dead," the newspaper said adding that the assailants cut the throats of the peasants, slaughtered their sheep and cows and stole the women's jewels.
Four women kidnapped during the massacre were later found dead with their throats slashed, El Watan said.
The newspaper said 17 people, including eight women, were slaughtered five days earlier at another village some five km (three miles) away.
Another newspaper, Al Khabar, said that last Monday rebels cut the throats of four people in Al Azharia village near Chlef, 150 km (95 miles) southwest of Algiers.

The reported recent flare-up in violence followed the June 5 general election which President Liamine Zeroual and legal opposition parties hope will help pacify the North African country after more than five years of violence.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
The authorities barred radical Islamists from this month's election but allowed two moderate Islamist parties to compete. These won a total of 103 seats in the 380-member National Assembly.
